title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 182 (Agent and principal defined)

content.overview: Section 182 provides that an ‘agent’ is a person employed to do any act for another, or to represent another in dealings with third persons. The person for whom such act is done, or who is so represented, is called the ‘principal’.
content.glance: An agent is a person employed to do any act for another or to represent another in dealings with third persons. The person for whom the act is done or who is represented is the principal.
content.study: An ‘agent’ is a person employed to do any act for another, or to represent another in dealings with third persons. The person for whom such act is done, or who is so represented, is called the ‘principal’. Current-law framing: foundational definition of the agency relationship under Chapter X.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.body: An ‘agent’ is a person employed to do any act for another, or to represent another in dealings with third persons. The person for whom such act is done, or who is so represented, is called the ‘principal’.

examples.title: Employment to act or represent
examples.body: A employs B to buy goods on A’s behalf or to represent A in dealings with third persons. B is the agent; A is the principal under Section 182.

hypotheticals.question: A person is employed to represent another in dealings with third persons. Who is the agent and who is the principal?
hypotheticals.analysis: The person employed is the agent; the person represented is the principal, under Section 182.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 182 defines an agent as a person employed to do any act for another, or to represent another in dealings with third persons. The person for whom such act is done, or who is so represented, is called the principal. This is the foundational definition for the law of agency in Chapter X.
examples: A person hired to buy or sell on behalf of another, or to represent that other to third parties, is an agent.
distinctions: Agency involves representation or acting for another; distinct from independent contracts or employment in other senses.
problemApplication: Identify employment to act for or represent another.

keyTakeaways: Agent is employed to do an act for or represent another (the principal).

distinctions.title: Scope of Section 182
distinctions.body: Section 182 applies only to the circumstances described in its statutory text. It does not create additional grounds or remedies beyond those stated.
